svg.title: DerivPort — Algorithm builder
svg.desc: Editable quantitative research interface with verified historical AAPL inputs, a balanced ranking rule, exact sensitivity, calculus explanations and an unrun historical backtest.

g.text: Write a ranking rule. Inspect the math. Test it on historical outcomes.
Fixed starting weights; no claim that they are optimal.
Scores rank stocks; they are not return forecasts.
Vary k while all four AAPL inputs stay fixed.
Tangent · coincides for a linear rule
Explore slope, curvature, and the accumulated change in your ranking score.
The linear and quadratic approximations match this linear rule.
Shaded area from 1 to 1.5: score change −2.9544.
T₂(Δk) = g(k₀) + g′(k₀) Δk + ½ g″(k₀) Δk²
A second-order Taylor approximation adds curvature to the local tangent.
The fundamental theorem links derivative area to score change.
These derivatives describe your rule. They do not measure the regression model’s feature influence.
Same group and periods for every algorithm
Run a historical test to see results.
Only complete 21-session periods count. No test has been run in this design state.
Rules selected or tuned after seeing outcomes are retrospective experiments.
Historical results do not guarantee future performance.
